title: How an interview goes
summary: What Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Atlassian and Flipkart say on their own careers pages about their interview loops and design rounds, with the page date, plus the companies that have no readable official guidance.

claims.text: Amazon's SDE II preparation page (no date shown) says the loop has four 55-minute interviews, each with members of its software development community.
Amazon's SDE II preparation page (no date shown) says to expect at least one question on software systems design.
Amazon's SDE II preparation page (no date shown) describes the online assessment as 90 minutes for two technical questions followed by 20 minutes of Systems Design scenarios.
Amazon's SDE III page (no date shown) lists five 55-minute interviews in the loop.
Amazon's SDE III page (no date shown) says the technical phone screen is with a senior leader on the team and lasts 60 minutes.
Meta's hiring process page (no date shown) says the process usually consists of a recruiter conversation, an initial screening and a full loop interview.
Meta's hiring process page (no date shown) says the typical process takes about 2 to 3 months.
Meta's technical screen page (no date shown) describes the initial tech screen as a 45-minute conversation with an engineer.
Atlassian's P30 to P50 backend guide (no date shown, file metadata 2023) lists two coding interviews, one system design interview, one management interview and a values interview.
The same Atlassian guide (no date shown, file metadata 2023) gives timings of 60 minutes for system design, 60 minutes for management and 45 minutes for values.
Flipkart's SDE guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) names a design round, round 2.3, that involves discussing and solving a non-trivial design problem.

sections.heading: How long a system design round is

claims.text: Meta's blog post (6 Oct 2022, page says updated for 2022) says the design interview is 45 minutes long and almost never involves coding.
Atlassian's Principal Backend guide (no date shown, file metadata 2023) says the system design portion of the interview is 60 minutes.
Flipkart's SDE guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) gives the design round as 60 minutes.
Flipkart's Architect guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) gives a 60-minute high-level design round, with 1 or 2 scenarios that need a fully detailed architectural solution.
Microsoft's technical interviewing page (no date shown) calls its interview round short at 45 minutes. The page does not tie the 45 minutes to system design.
Amazon's SDE II preparation page (no date shown) says the loop has four 55-minute interviews. The page gives this length for each loop interview and does not give a length for design alone.
Amazon's SDE III page (no date shown) says the loop has five 55-minute interviews. The page gives this length for each loop interview and does not give a length for design alone.

sections.heading: What interviewers say they look for

claims.text: Meta (blog, 6 Oct 2022, page says updated for 2022) says the purpose of the design interview is to assess the candidate's ability to solve a non-trivial engineering design problem.
Meta's blog (6 Oct 2022) says a good solution compares and contrasts different approaches.
Meta's blog (6 Oct 2022) adds that the ability to anticipate and work around typical problems is part of the signal.
Amazon's SDE II page (no date shown) lists these objectives: practicality, accuracy, efficiency, reliability, optimization and scalability.
Amazon's software development topics page (no date shown) says interviewers look for the ability to apply what you know to solve problems efficiently and effectively.
Microsoft's technical interviewing page (no date shown) says knowledge of distributed systems, SOA and n-tiered software architecture is very important for system design questions.
Microsoft's technical interviewing page (no date shown) says resiliency, high availability, auto-scaling, replication, CAP theory and partitioning may all be included.
Microsoft's technical interviewing page (no date shown) says candidates should understand what it takes to build or design a new system or platform from scratch.
Atlassian's Principal Backend guide (no date shown) says the interviewer looks at problem-solving thought process, decision making and operational considerations.
The Atlassian Principal Backend guide (no date shown) tells candidates to keep the customer in mind and how the solution might perform and scale.

Flipkart's SDE guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) expects a scalable system with the trade-offs needed to achieve that, and knowledge of different types of data stores and when to choose one over another.

In its general interview tips, Flipkart's SDE guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) says: "We don't necessarily look for absolute solutions." It adds that the interviewers want to know how you approach a problem.

Flipkart's Architect guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) lists tech stack selection, scalability of the solution, and choosing between consistency, availability and partition tolerance as separate evaluation pivots.

Meta's blog (6 Oct 2022, page says updated for 2022) says to start with requirements. Its example is how to architect the backend for a messaging system, and it lists questions to ask about how many people, how many messages, latency, storage, and push or pull.
Microsoft's technical interviewing page (no date shown) says to ask clarifying questions about any ambiguities and come up with a plan before implementing a solution.
Microsoft's interview tips page (no date shown) says to start by asking clarifying questions and stating your assumptions, then talk through your approach, including the tools you would use and why.
Atlassian's P30 to P50 guide (no date shown) describes starting with fundamentals and then building in complexity, and asking any clarifying questions upfront.
Flipkart's SDE guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) says the problem will be very generic and tells candidates to start by gathering all the specific requirements from the interviewer.
Amazon's SDE II page (no date shown) says the interviewer will ask questions related to your design, and that you should ask questions to complete and validate your design.
Meta's blog (6 Oct 2022, page says updated for 2022) says the interviewer asks a very broad design problem and evaluates the solution.
Meta's blog (6 Oct 2022) asks candidates to make it a conversation, ask clarifying questions, and drive towards a good solution.
Meta's blog (6 Oct 2022) says there is not enough time to discuss every detail, and advises finding the interesting and hard problems to focus the discussion on.
Atlassian's P30 to P50 guide (no date shown) tells candidates to keep communicating with the interviewer as they progress towards a solution.
Flipkart's SDE guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) describes the round as the interviewer and interviewee discussing trade-offs and requirements and coming up with a solution.
Flipkart's SDE guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) says the design round is about discussing different approaches at different stages and zeroing in on one.
Flipkart's Architect guide (no date shown, file metadata 2020) asks candidates to be vocal about multiple acceptable solutions, and specifically why they rejected the others.
Meta's hiring process page (no date shown) says design interviews are conducted in CoderPad with Mermaid Markdown, with the same AI assistant available as in the coding interview.
Amazon's software development topics page (no date shown) says most technical interviews require coding and system design white boarding exercises.

noGuidance.note: The how-we-hire interview page returned 200, but its text is drawn by JavaScript. The raw page held only navigation and footer; nothing could be confirmed.

Uber's careers pages and jobs.uber.com returned HTTP 403 or 406 to curl. The one readable Uber page, an engineering blog post from 8 Dec 2015, covers the hiring market and does not cover the design round.
Rubrik's careers page returned 403 to curl, and no other official page was found.
The Netflix Tech Blog interview post returned 403 on netflixtechblog.com and on medium.com. The jobs.netflix.com new-grad page was not read.
No interview process page was found.
The stripe.com/jobs/interview address is a 404, and no candidate-facing system design page was found.
The careers FAQ gives a 60 to 75 minute Craft Assessment but never names system design; it is not used.
